explanation: This slide presents two autosomal recessive disorders: Methemoglobinemia and Cystic Fibrosis. Methemoglobinemia is a relatively harmless disorder in which the accumulation of methemoglobin in the blood causes the skin to look bluish-purple. Cystic Fibrosis is a severe disorder characterized by thick and viscous mucus that builds up in the bronchial tubes and pancreatic ducts.

questions.q: What causes the skin of individuals with methemoglobinemia to appear bluish-purple?
opts: Accumulation of methemoglobin in the blood.
Low counts of red blood cells.
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the slide explains: 'Accumulation of methemoglobin in the blood causes skin to appear bluish-purple'.

questions.q: What is the physiological hallmark of Cystic Fibrosis mentioned on the slide?
opts: Accumulation of methemoglobin in the blood.
Spherical red blood cells that burst easily.
Extremely thick and viscous mucus in bronchial tubes and pancreatic ducts.
Synthesis of abnormal type I collagen.
questions.exp: Option C is correct because the slide explains Cystic Fibrosis as: 'Mucus in bronchial tubes and pancreatic ducts is particularly thick and viscous'.
